run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T05:58:17Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert tracks frontend-proxy error-status spans, and that service is demonstrably returning 5xx responses while its own pods are up. The only app metric in this target is `traces_span_metrics_calls_total`; for service_name="frontend-proxy" the `ingress` (server) STATUS_CODE_ERROR counter rose from 424 at 05:28:17Z to 444 at 06:06:17Z against 6151→30563 UNSET ingress spans, and the peak 5-min increase was 7.78 error spans (05:41Z). At 05:58:17Z the 5-minute error-to-span ratio was 0.00038, so the alert annotation's 0.0111 is closest to the absolute per-second error rate (3.33 errors per 5 min = 0.0111/s), i.e. the rule appears to fire on a very small but non-zero error rate. The retained Envoy access logs explain what the errors are: 10 of 11,442 access-log lines between 05:46:05Z and 06:03:10Z are `503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}` with upstream cluster `frontend` (paths /api/cart, /api/products/*, /api/data, /api/recommendations). So the immediate failure is the frontend upstream terminating the connection before response headers, surfacing as 503s at frontend-proxy. The frontend Deployment runs with a 100m CPU limit, its pod was pinned at ~0.09-0.10 cores with 21-31% CFS throttling, and neither frontend nor frontend-proxy has a readiness probe; however throttling is namespace-wide, the frontend records no error spans of its own, and no per-request link between throttling and the resets was observed, so the reason the frontend terminates connections remains a hypothesis rather than an established cause. All pods are Running/ready with 0 restarts and populated endpoints, and no OOM/Evicted events exist, so crashes, evictions and missing endpoints are not supported. Other entities checked: frontend, frontend-proxy pods and Services are up; ad, fraud-detection and recommendation show only low-level background error spans (≤~1.5 per 5 min) not tied to this path.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's span metrics contain STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans: its `ingress` error counter went from 424 at 05:28:17Z to 444 at 06:06:17Z while `ingress` STATUS_CODE_UNSET went from 6151 to 30563; the `router frontend egress` error counter stayed flat at 396.

Ten 5xx access-log lines from pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-4dlth between 05:48:06Z and 06:01:56Z are all `503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}` on upstream cluster `frontend`, for paths /api/cart, /api/products/LS4PSXUNUM, /api/products/66VCHSJNUP, /api/products/2ZYFJ3GM2N, /api/products/L9ECAV7KIM, /api/data/?contextKeys=books, /api/data/?contextKeys=binoculars, /api/data/?contextKeys=travel and /api/recommendations.

The error rate observed in the proxy's own access logs is low: 10 of 11,442 in-window access-log lines (4 of 4,019 lines in 05:46:05-05:52:00, 6 of 7,423 lines in 05:52:00-06:03:10) were 5xx, about 0.6 errors/min against roughly 11 requests/s.

At the alert time 2026-11-17T05:58:17Z the 5-minute ratio sum(rate(frontend-proxy STATUS_CODE_ERROR))/sum(rate(frontend-proxy all spans)) was 0.00038, while the 5-minute error-span increase peaked at 7.78 spans around 05:41Z (3.33 per 5 min = 0.0111/s at 05:38Z).

Deployment `frontend` sets container frontend cpu limit 100m / request 50m and has readinessProbe=null and livenessProbe=null; Deployment `frontend-proxy` sets cpu limit 30m / request 15m and also has no readiness or liveness probe.

Pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2 was pinned at ~0.09-0.10 cores of its 100m limit from 05:30Z to 06:07Z, its CFS throttled-period ratio was 21-31% throughout that period, and its working set grew from 121.8 MB to 132.1 MB against a 200Mi limit.
Pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-4dlth used ~0.026 cores of its 30m limit and was 4-6% CFS-throttled over the same period.

CPU throttling is namespace-wide, not unique to frontend: at 05:58:17Z the highest throttled-period ratios were frontend 0.293, postgresql 0.273, cart 0.200, product-catalog 0.178, quote 0.129, payment 0.118, ad 0.117 and frontend-proxy 0.043.

All 21 otel-demo pods were Running and ready with restartCount 0; frontend-675fd7b5c5-5vnt2 was created 05:17:19Z (owner ReplicaSet frontend-675fd7b5c5, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend) and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-4dlth 05:17:18Z (owner ReplicaSet frontend-proxy-6b4d584985, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend-proxy).
The frontend Service and the frontend-proxy Service both have populated endpoints (frontend 8080 at 100.96.2.93, frontend-proxy 8080 at 100.96.2.11).

The only events recorded for namespace otel-demo inside the window are the load-generator rollout at 05:49:07-05:49:08Z (Deployment load-generator ScalingReplicaSet, ReplicaSet load-generator-84895ffcd SuccessfulCreate / load-generator-57ffcd644 SuccessfulDelete, Pod load-generator-84895ffcd-hp7pb Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started and Pod load-generator-57ffcd644-8ft89 Killing).
The event groups returned across all namespaces contain no Pod reason Evicted and no OOMKilling group.

frontend's own STATUS_CODE_ERROR span counter increase was 0 at every sampled point from 05:29Z to 06:07Z, while ad (≤1.50), fraud-detection (≤1.23) and recommendation (≤1.11) showed small nonzero increases and frontend-proxy peaked at 7.78 per 5 minutes.

ConfigMap flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) sets loadGeneratorFloodHomepage defaultVariant "on" ("Flood the frontend with a large amount of requests"), while every other listed fault flag (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) is "off".

Jaeger held traces for service frontend only around 05:31:33-05:31:35Z in this Run; the 5 traces sampled there are all 200/308 with error_rows 0, and frontend-proxy ingress spans in that sample are http.status_code 200/308, not 5xx.

frontend-proxy exposes exactly two span operations, `ingress` (SPAN_KIND_SERVER) and `router frontend egress` (SPAN_KIND_CLIENT), so the ingress ERROR spans are the server-side responses returned to clients.

The 503s originate at the frontend upstream: Envoy reports connection_termination before response headers on cluster `frontend`, so the frontend server is closing/resetting the connection. A plausible trigger is the frontend container's 100m CPU quota with continuous 21-31% CFS throttling delaying/dropping connections, but no per-request link between a throttled period and a 503 was observed.

Because frontend and frontend-proxy declare no readiness probes, Kubernetes made them Ready as soon as the containers started, so the load generator could hit them before the Next.js server was accepting connections; this would explain the dense error accumulation already present at the first metric sample (424 ingress and 396 egress error spans by 05:28:17Z, right after the 05:17Z rollout).

An alternative trigger for the steady trickle of 503s is an upstream keep-alive reuse race (the frontend closes an idle HTTP keep-alive connection just as Envoy sends a request), which yields exactly `upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}` at a low rate; no Envoy admin stats or keep-alive timeout settings are available here to confirm it.

The frontend's own span metrics record no error spans, and its pod has restartCount 0, so the frontend did not report its own failures; the failing evidence exists on the caller side (frontend-proxy 503s and the Envoy upstream detail), not in frontend telemetry.

The load-generator rollout at 05:49:07Z is not the onset of the errors: the frontend-proxy ingress error counter was already 424 at 05:28:17Z (about 21 minutes before the rollout, and before the retained logs begin), and the frontend CPU level and request rate did not step at 05:49Z.
Pod crash, OOM or eviction is not the cause: every otel-demo pod is Running and ready with restartCount 0, and the returned event groups contain no Evicted or OOMKilling reason.

A missing or unreachable upstream endpoint is not supported: the frontend Service resolves to endpoint 100.96.2.93:8080 and the frontend-proxy Service to 100.96.2.11:8080, and Envoy reached the upstream far enough to observe a connection termination on it.

Retrieve the RequestErrorRate rule expression from the Alertmanager/Prometheus rule store outside this target; list_prometheus_rules returned no rules here, and the annotation value 0.0111 could not be reproduced as a ratio (measured 5-min ratio 0.00038), so the exact threshold and denominator should be confirmed.

Raise the frontend container CPU limit above 100m (or lower load) and add readiness/liveness probes to frontend and frontend-proxy so traffic is not routed before the apps listen; then verify whether the 503 UC rate falls.

Review why flagd flag loadGeneratorFloodHomepage is "on" (it declares a homepage request flood) and whether the load-generator's restart at 05:49Z changed its behaviour, since a flood amplifies load on the CPU-capped frontend.

Collect Envoy upstream statistics (upstream_rq_reset, upstream_cx_connect_fail, upstream_rq_pending_overflow) and the frontend HTTP keep-alive settings to distinguish connection-reset races from CPU-starvation resets.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate rule definition is not retrievable: list_prometheus_rules returned no rules (both filtered and unfiltered queries were empty), so the alert's exact expression, threshold and evaluation window are unknown and its 0.0111 annotation could not be reproduced as a ratio.

No usable baseline: despite a 24-hour-authorized query, the frontend-proxy span-metric series returned samples only from ~05:28Z/05:38Z onward (the 24h query returned just three points at 05:38Z, 05:53Z, 06:08Z), so earlier history is unavailable and no pre-incident error-rate baseline exists.

Jaeger did not return error spans for frontend-proxy: traces_search_by_tags for service=frontend-proxy with error=true and with http.status_code="503" (05:00-05:32Z) returned nothing, and traces_search for frontend-proxy returned nothing for 05:50-06:08Z; the newest trace data returned in this Run was ~05:31:35Z, so per-request trace detail and the http.status_code tag of the failing requests remain unknown.
frontend's container produced no log lines in the queried windows (05:46:05-06:03:10Z returned 0 bytes), so no application-side confirmation of why connections are reset is available.
Kubernetes pod logs are only retained from ~05:46:08Z to ~06:03:03Z for frontend-proxy, so the dense early error burst (before 05:28Z) cannot be inspected.

kube-state-metrics series are absent from this Prometheus: queries for kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready (and the kube_* names in the metric inventory) returned nothing, so Deployment-level ready/available readings at 05:58Z could not be checked; pod state at query time is the only workload-status evidence.
Queries for networkpolicies and resourcequotas in otel-demo returned no objects; no conclusion about policy-based blocking can be drawn from that.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so whether the frontend CPU limit, the missing probes, or the flagd configuration were changed before the incident cannot be verified.

The load-generator pod template changed at 05:49:07Z (new ReplicaSet load-generator-84895ffcd, same image tag ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-load-generator); the previous pod spec/env is not retrievable, so what changed in that rollout is unknown.
Why the request stream and CPU usage dropped to near zero around 06:00-06:03Z (span counters flat after 06:01Z, frontend CPU 0.10→0.004 cores) is not established from the available evidence.
next_steps: Read the RequestErrorRate alerting rule and its records from the Alertmanager/Prometheus rule store that owns it, and confirm whether it measures a ratio or an absolute error rate.
Inspect the frontend application logs from inside the container (its stdout is currently empty) and compare Envoy upstream reset counters with frontend CPU throttling periods.
Test raising the frontend CPU limit and adding readiness probes in a staging copy, and observe whether 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} disappears.
Confirm the intended state of flagd flag loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and of the load-generator configuration changed at 05:49Z.
